adherence.reason: The story centers on investigating a repeated phrase across suspicious death notices and identifying a killer.
The first-person protagonist, Elias Thorne, explicitly works as the obituary writer for the small Oakhaven Chronicle.
Elias finds the identical heavy-heart phrase in the notices for Harriet Gable, Leo Vance, and Thomas Alcott, described as unrelated deaths.
The narration explicitly reveals the phrase as the killer's signature claiming murders disguised as accidents.
The narrator says he has worked for fifteen years and never met half the deceased, rather than being a woman with over fifteen years who has not met most of them.
Much of the story occurs in the nearly empty newspaper office, but substantial scenes move to a funeral home and outside in the storm.
The opening explicitly places events in the quiet interval between Christmas and New Year's.
The narrative remains in first person from obituary writer Elias's point of view.
Elias drafts his own obituary as a trap and waits for the killer to alter it, but explicitly says he did not submit the edit request, so the required final trap mechanism is only partial.
